title: How to Open a Presentation So People Keep Watching (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Open so people keep watching
slides.notes: The first thirty seconds decide whether people lean in or reach for their phones. On video, one click and they're gone. Here's how to open well.

slides.title: Cut what slows the opening
bullets: The agenda slide as slide two
slides.notes: Before adding anything, remove what slows you down. Viewers don't need an agenda, your full bio or an apology before they know why they care.

slides.title: Five openings that hook viewers
bullets: A short story or a surprising, true detail
slides.notes: Name a problem they already feel, give away the result first, or ask a specific question. A short real story or a true detail works too.

slides.title: Lead with the point, not the agenda
bullets: Before: title, About me, Agenda, Background
After: "Shorter reminder emails got more replies"
slides.notes: Instead of thanks, introductions and project history, open with the finding. The viewer knows the point and the plan in under twenty seconds.

slides.title: Make the first slide work hard
bullets: A headline that states the point
Large text that reads on a phone
"In the next five minutes, you'll see three changes"
slides.notes: Make the first slide state the point, then promise what's coming. Keep that first spoken line short, and match it to the headline on screen.

slides.title: Hear your opening before anyone else
bullets: Write the opening into the speaker notes
Rewrite the first slide and try again
slides.notes: Write your opening into the speaker notes and turn the deck into video at powerpoint2vid.com. Try Basic first; on Pro, a.i. directs, landing your first line on a designed scene.
